key_insight: The paper proposes that an LLM’s capacity for scientific discovery is governed by “monofacts”—facts encountered exactly once during training. It connects these rare observations to missing probability mass: knowledge not represented in the training sample.
problem_solved: How can we trace an LLM’s ability to make scientific discoveries back to measurable properties of its training data?
method: Frame scientific discovery using missing probability mass, representing facts absent from the training sample.
Develop a theoretical account linking discovery capacity to the rate of monofacts in training data.
Directly manipulate monofact rates in materials science and regulatory genomics; the provided abstract is truncated before reporting experimental outcomes.
impact: This framework could help practitioners assess discovery potential through training-data composition, rather than model size alone. It suggests that rare facts deserve attention when designing scientific training datasets.
visual_elements: Training-data frequency histogram highlighting facts observed exactly once.
Conceptual diagram connecting monofact rate, missing probability mass, and discovery capacity.
Side-by-side materials science and regulatory genomics panels illustrating the study domains.
Dataset comparison showing low versus high monofact rates, without implying unreported performance results.
paper_title: Tracing the Scientific Discovery Capacity of LLMs to Their Training Data
paper_authors: Arda Uzunoglu, Mahler Revsine, Michael Schatz, Benjamin Van Durme, Mehrdad Farajtabar
